Series::retains_grad¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::retains_grad() const -> Series

What It Does¶

retains_grad() reports whether this Series is currently marked to keep its stored sensitivity after reverse-mode runs.

One public-surface quirk matters immediately: this method returns a scalar boolean Series, not a plain bool. In ordinary C++ use, most callers read it with .item<bool>().

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series A scalar boolean Series indicating whether retention is enabled on this value.

Relationship To Nearby Methods¶

  • retain_grad() changes this state

  • retains_grad() reads this state

  • has_sensitivity() asks whether a stored sensitivity currently exists

Those are different questions:

  • one is configuration

  • one is current stored data presence

Mathematical Meaning¶

Suppose mid is an intermediate value in a computation with scalar objective L.

If retention is enabled, then after reverse-mode finishes, mid is allowed to keep the stored quantity

dL/dmid

If retention is disabled, that same quantity may still exist transiently during propagation, but it is not kept as a public stored result afterward.

So retains_grad() is not asking whether the derivative exists mathematically. It is asking whether the object is configured to keep that derivative around for later inspection.

Examples¶

Example 1. Intermediates do not start in retain mode by default.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
auto mid = x.mul(3.0);

std::cout << "before=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
mid.retain_grad();
std::cout << "after=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

before=false
after=true

Example 2. Turning retention off again is reflected immediately.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
auto mid = x.mul(4.0);
mid.retain_grad(false);

std::cout << "retains=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

retains=false

Example 3. Retention state and stored-sensitivity presence are related but not identical.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto mid = x.mul(2.0);
mid.retain_grad();

std::cout << "retains=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "mid_has_dL_dmid=" << (mid.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

At this point retention is enabled, but no reverse pass has run yet, so the intermediate still has no stored sensitivity.

Output¶

retains=true
mid_has_dL_dmid=false

Example 4. After reverse runs, a retained intermediate can both report retention and hold stored sensitivity.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto mid = x.mul(2.0);
mid.retain_grad();
mid.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "retains=" << (mid.retains_grad().item<bool>() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "mid_has_dL_dmid=" << (mid.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

For

mid = 2x
L = sum(mid)

the reverse pass computes dL/dmid = [1, 1, 1]. Because retention is enabled, that intermediate sensitivity is kept.

Output¶

retains=true
mid_has_dL_dmid=true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • retains_grad() returns a scalar Series, not a plain bool.

  • retains_grad() == true does not by itself mean reverse-mode has already populated stored sensitivity. It only means the keep-state is enabled.

  • Use has_sensitivity() when you need to know whether a stored sensitivity currently exists.

Summary¶

Use retains_grad() to inspect whether a Series is configured to keep its stored sensitivity after reverse, and read it as a boolean scalar with .item<bool>() in ordinary C++ code.

See Also¶

  • Series::retain_grad: enable or disable the keep-state.

  • Series::has_sensitivity: check whether stored sensitivity currently exists.
